spec.title: Conventions

item.title: Contents lists and examples in every markdown file
No agent prose to agent prose

spec.purpose: The rules every file, script, seat and record in this repo follows, so an agent never has to ask how to name, time, log or configure something.

section.title: Naming
section.text: Tickets: WO-YYYYMMDD-xxxx, always written with their full title in any reply. Branches: feat/<slug>, chore/<slug>, fix/<slug>. Graph nodes: PREFIX-slug (SPEC-00). Specs: SPEC-NN-<slug>.xml. herdr workspace label = repo name; tab label = seat name or tab group name; pane label = <kind> - <what> [ticket], for example "test - bearings WO-20261010-ba08", "bearings-uat-WO-20261010-ba08", "MONITOR - event-log". Seat names: <role>-<ticket> lowercased, under 32 chars. Pages: <project>-<tier>[-<ticket>].

node.title: Every AGENTS.md and markdown file is runtime-agnostic, opens with a contents list, carries GOOD and NEVER examples

section.title: Time
section.text: UTC everywhere an agent writes: logs, filenames, tickets, ledgers, checkpoints, graph nodes, specs. Format YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MMZ in attributes and filenames; ISO 8601 with seconds in JSON records. Only the owner's Windows clock stays local.

section.title: Contents lists and examples in every markdown file
section.text: Every AGENTS.md, README, runbook, SOP, playbook and spec opens with a Contents list of its H2 headings in order. Every rule carries at least two GOOD and two NEVER examples. Instructions name roles and runtimes generically: "the worker seat", "a Claude runtime", "a Codex runtime", "a System One runtime (Jev, Layla)"; a file that only works for one runtime says so in its first line. AGENTS.md is the binding file; CLAUDE.md is a pointer to it and nothing else.

section.title: Config and variables

node.title: Nothing hardcoded: every tunable in versioned schema-validated config, S3-portable, variables resolved at load

section.text: Every tunable (model id, effort, port, path, label, threshold, retry count, timeout, URL) lives in a JSON or YAML file with a schema_version field and a JSON schema beside it. Strings may carry ${HOME}, ${project}, ${tier}, ${ticket}, ${ENV:NAME}; the loader resolves them and fails with exit 3 naming an unknown one. No absolute path or hostname inside a config file, so the file can be lifted into S3 unchanged. No script carries a default: a missing key is exit 3 naming the key. Secrets come from Vault through ${ENV:NAME}, never from a file in git.

section.title: Entry points

node.title: Makefiles are the entry point of every repo in this project

section.text: Every directory with executable code has a Makefile; make help lists targets. Standard targets: build, lint, test, image, serve, stop, status, clean. A target is a thin call into a script; logic lives in the script so the same thing runs from a pane, a Jenkinsfile and a container. Skills in dotfiles keep their justfile (dotfiles Rule 17).

section.title: Status codes

node.title: HTTP-shaped status codes from rime: 100 ACCEPTED, 200 DONE, 201 PASSED, 300 ROUTED, 412 GATE_FAILED, 422 FAILED, 423 BLOCKED, 429, 500
compaction-guard families GOV, CMP, RES, RCV, OPS: 1xx-2xx normal, 3xx controller, 4xx pushback, 5xx recovery

section.text: Every record a node, seat, gate or monitor emits carries one code. Factory records use the HTTP-shaped set; governance records use the guard families. 3 attempts then 423 BLOCKED; a 423 goes to the architect once; a second 423 on the same ticket is an owner card. A code is machine-routed (SPEC-03); a human-readable note is at most 240 chars and never the thing a script branches on.

section.title: Event log

node.title: One git-tracked event log dir, one file per entry, status code and UTC only, multi-agent safe

section.text: events/YYYY/MM/<UTC>-<code>-<suffix>.json, one file per entry, written by one script (events/bin/event.sh add --code 423 --seat worker-ba08 --ticket WO-... --note "..."). Distinct filenames mean N writers never collide and git never conflicts. Only important items: a code at or above 300, a seat up or down, a gate result, a merge, a compaction. Routine progress is a ledger line, not an event. events/bin/event.sh check validates every file; the monitor seat tails the directory in its own tab group (SPEC-04). Nothing in an entry is prose from one agent to another.

section.title: No agent prose to agent prose

node.title: Every factory node: schema in, schema out, 3 retries, black box, no agent prose to agent prose

section.text: A seat hands the next seat a record (ticket id, status code, evidence paths, observations array), never a paragraph. The only prose in the system goes to the owner, on the page, one or two lines plus a link. Briefs to a seat are one line naming the ticket and the playbook to read. Kickback on error is a script: evidence.sh --ticket --code --observed --repro --screenshot, which writes the record and wakes the architect.

section.title: Code style

node.title: Functional programming mindset: pure functions, side effects at the edges, easy to test, frameworks and the right tool for the job, Makefile targets
Test plans, harnesses and records are generated by scripts from templates; hand-writing them is not token efficient

section.text: Logic is pure where it can be: a function takes values and returns values, and the file system, network, herdr socket and clock are touched only in a thin outer layer that a test can replace. Every verb is a script with an input and an output, testable from a Makefile target in Podman. Use the framework that already solves the problem (Playwright for browsers, jsonschema for config, gRPC for machine-to-machine, Harmony for Unity mods) instead of a hand-rolled substitute. Anything written more than once is a template rendered by a script: test suites, test plans, tickets, seat briefs, event records.
